Le regole dovranno essere rappresentate in una matrice univoca tra linea, prerequisito, evidenza, soglia, badge, gate, recupero e percorso successivo. 8. Dimensionamento e famiglie di format 8.1 Dimensionamento della componente produttiva Per ciascuno dei cinque percorsi oggetto di produzione, l’Offerente dovrà quantificare nella Proposta didattica preliminare gli output digitali e i materiali previsti, indicando almeno quantità aggregate, durata o estensione media, livello di complessità, modalità di fruizione e dipendenze produttive. Le quantità relative a webinar, lezioni in presenza, assessment e incontri individuali indicate nei template costituiscono riferimenti di architettura didattica. L’Offerente dovrà separare chiaramente i prodotti da realizzare dagli eventi da progettare e successivamente erogare da Formaper. 8.2 Famiglie di format utilizzabili Famiglia Finalità prevalente Video didattici e microlearning Introduzione, spiegazione, dimostrazione, casi e consolidamento. ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NATIONAL DIGITAL SKILLS TRAINING PROGRAMME (NDSTP)

 

The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority – Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project – Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy services for the implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP)

responsibility of implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP) programme across Uganda. The assignment will equip at least 6,000 beneficiaries drawn from public servants, teachers and tutors, out-of-school youth, refugees and refugee-host communities, and persons with disabilities with the digital knowledge and practical competencies needed to access services safely and productively, pursue education and livelihood opportunities, and participate as informed digital citizens.

The duration of the assignment will be five (5) months from the date of contract signing.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be accessed at https://www.nita.go.ug

Website Hosting & Support Service The objective of this tender process is to invite proposals for the provision of website hosting, ongoing maintenance and development services for the CORU website. Tenderers shall demonstrate their capability to provide a secure, reliable, and resilient hosting environment that supports the continued availability and performance of the website. Particular consideration will be given to: • The location of the hosting infrastructure and the suitability of the hosting arrangement from a regulatory, operational, and data governance perspective. • The provision of secure and user -friendly content management functionality that enables authorised CORU staff to undertake routine and moderate website content updates without requiring specialist technical support. • The implementation of appropriate security controls, monitoring, and maintenance processes to protect the website from unauthorised access, modification, disruption, or malicious activi

Website Migration Services The successful tenderer shall be responsible for the migration of CORU's existing live website to the proposed hosting environment. The migration service shall include, at a minimum: • Development and execution of a detailed migration plan, including timelines, responsibilities, testing and implementation activities. • Migration of all website content, functionality, configurations and associated assets to the proposed environment. • Measures to minimise disruption to website availability and user experience during the migration process. • Comprehensive testing prior to go -live, including functional, security, performance, accessibility and user acceptance testing. • Provision of rollback and recovery procedures in the event of migration issues. • Preservation of existing search engine rankings and implementation of any necessary redirects and SEO protections during migration. • Post-migration support to address any issues arising following implementation. insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed primarily at the contractors facilit

Requirements/Salient Characteristics: The following specification lists the minimum requirements for a lock-in amplifier. Objective requirements are also highlighted when available. A lock-in amplifier is crucial for separating laser photodetector outputs from noise that may otherwise drown out the signal. Therefore, this lock-in component is necessary for meeting mission requirements. 3.1. The lock-in amplifier shall meet the following technical requirements: 3.1.1. Demodulation capability for DC up to 600 megahertz or higher reference signals 3.1.2. At least two analog BNC inputs 3.1.3. At least two analog BNC outputs 3.1.4. Analog to digital input conversion capability included, along with the inverse of digital to analog output conversion 3.1.5. Minimum sampling rate for input data of 1.25 giga-samples per second (GSa/s) 3.1.6. USB 2.0 or USB-C interface is supported 3.1.7. PC software interface included 3.1.8. Coding support for either Python or MATLAB languages 3.1.8.1. API for supported language must be given 3.1.9. Come with a manufacturer’s warranty of at least 1 year 3.1.10. Signal output must support digital to analog conversion of at least 1.25 giga-s
